claims.title: Pathwise affine regret attains its maximum at a bounded-TV path vertex
claims.scope: finite affine path-decision and comparator families over one finite-horizon rational bounded-TV source-law path polytope
assumptions: each decision cost is affine in the complete source-law path
the comparator family is finite
the path polytope is compact and its bounded vertex enumeration completes
nonclaims: the result does not cover an arbitrary nonlinear path cost without another convexity or finite reduction argument
bounded vertex enumeration is not a large-scale complexity guarantee

claims.title: Shared-randomness pathwise regret reduces to an exact finite zero-sum game
claims.scope: source-independent common mixtures of finite affine open-loop decisions against a finite comparator family over the bounded-TV path polytope
assumptions: the source path is selected independently of the realized shared seed
all required decoders know the realized decision
exact rational game support enumeration completes
nonclaims: private encoder randomness is not substituted for common randomness
the exact random-bit cost of sampling the rational mixture is not priced

claims.title: Comparator-class expansion monotonically increases pathwise regret
claims.scope: one fixed decision family and nested finite comparator families under the same path and cost model
assumptions: the larger comparator class contains the smaller comparator class
decision and comparator accounting use the same declared cost units
nonclaims: a stronger comparator is not itself an implementable causal policy
monotonicity does not imply a strict increase on every instance

claims.title: Robust value differences only bound pathwise regret
claims.scope: deterministic and source-independent shared mixtures of finite affine decisions over one compact path set
assumptions: the path-specific oracle minimum is finite on the path set
robust absolute costs and oracle extrema are computed under the same path set
nonclaims: the lower robust-value gap is not generally equal to regret
separately optimized maxima need not occur at the same path

claims.title: Exact zero-error code-sequence regret with distinct decision and comparator switch budgets
claims.scope: complete bounded deterministic zero-error binary-prefix codebooks, finite open-loop sequences, bounded TV source drift, and rational common switch cost
assumptions: the decision switch budget does not exceed the comparator switch budget
the decision family is contained in the comparator family
codebook, sequence, path, and game enumerations complete below their configured caps
nonclaims: the selected sequence is open-loop rather than feedback adaptive
the switch penalty is a declared design input rather than an inferred physical cost

claims.title: Full-drift binary prediction has deterministic regret T and shared regret T over two
claims.scope: binary source states, horizon T, eta=1, all binary action sequences, mismatch loss, and the same class used as the clairvoyant comparator
assumptions: the source path is chosen after the deterministic action sequence or source-independent shared mixture
each period source law may range over the full binary simplex
nonclaims: the closed values are specific to the declared mismatch-loss game
the result does not state the regret of a causal learning algorithm

claims.title: The path-specific oracle maximum is an exact maximin game and may be attained only in the interior
claims.scope: finite affine comparator families over one compact finite-horizon path polytope with an exact finite vertex representation
assumptions: each comparator cost is affine in the complete path
the path polytope equals the convex hull of its enumerated vertices
exact rational zero-sum game support enumeration completes
nonclaims: the maximizing vertex mixture is a proof representation of a feasible barycenter and need not describe physical randomization among paths
a concave oracle maximum is not generally obtained by taking the largest oracle value at a path vertex

claims.title: Bounded exact pathwise regret and value-gap audit
claims.scope: the finite rational path, decision, comparator, code-sequence, and zero-sum game instances exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured active-basis, sequence, candidate, and game support caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for every finite objective and feasibility calculation
nonclaims: CI success is not a scalability theorem
finite regret calculations are not evidence that reality is simulated
